title: A learned MRI model localizes known dysplasia lesions in FLAIR-negative images
summary: A convolutional model trained on lesion-image patterns was evaluated on 18 FLAIR-negative images from 12 patients with histologically confirmed focal cortical dysplasia. The source reports localization in 15 of the 18 images. This is a small retrospective lesion-localization result, not validated population screening or proof of improved surgical outcomes.
ai_technology: Net-Pos convolutional network; activation-maximization pattern localization
organization: Beijing Institute of Technology; Sixth Medical Center of PLA General Hospital

evidence.tested: The overall source dataset has 34 FLAIR images from 19 patients; the FLAIR-negative evaluation contains 18 images from 12 patients. CNN training/test image-block sets are described as coming from unique patients. Localization is compared with lesion regions marked using operative locations.
evidence.unknown: The abstract calls 15/18recall subject-wise, but its denominator is18 images from 12 patients; it is not presented here as 15 patients detected. Surgical/pathology-selected cases and marked lesion references do not establish accuracy in unselected MRI-negative epilepsy patients. The small dataset, image-block construction and modest segmentation overlap limit generalization; no independent clinical deployment is shown.
evidence.ai_role: A six-layer CNN learns lesion-associated image-block features; activation maximization derives representative patterns used to localize suspected lesions in FLAIR-negative images.

source_review.scope: Exact primary publisher title/DOI/date; relevant indexed primary cohort, learned-model and reference-validation Methods/Results and limitations. Fresh Crossref publication-status metadata, no linked update; direct full-page access limited.
